structured_output.summary: The household is one person, age 85 and disabled, with monthly gross income of $2,581.83. That is just under Wisconsin's FY2026 200% FPL limit of $2,610, so the household is broad-based categorically eligible and no net income test applies. Net income is roughly $2,000–$2,200 a month, so 30% of it is far above the $298 one-person maximum and the computed benefit is $0. As an eligible one-person household it gets the $24 minimum instead: $24 × 12 = $288. The engine reaches the same result. Its net income ($2,036) differs from stage 1's ($2,214), but either figure gives the minimum benefit. The FY2027 $25 minimum comes from a USDA memo dated 2026-08-21, after the freeze, so $24 is the correct amount for Oct–Dec under frozen law. The consensus answer of $0 applies only the regular elderly/disabled 100% FPL net income test and misses Wisconsin's broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE).
